comment: Epoch 64 of 1.3.0 (pending), EU5 1.4.7/build26377361; frozen epoch63 preserved in golden_world_epoch63.json. Wastelands are planned terrain, not the highest cells: dunes, plateaus, flat wilds under any vegetation, hills and mountains, chosen from the climate and vegetation just drawn, at the sea as inland, and sized from the vanilla impassable locations (rnw.barrens), and named for their terrain (a Highlands, a Wilds, a Desert). They are decided before the coasts, so the ports, docks and strait crossings are made for the land they leave passable. The active coasts raise cordilleras; the rivers are drawn before the land cells, which take the larger rivers as borders and are seeded as far apart as the game's locations of the class, ground and coast first cells voted as the final ones are will have, graded so that neighbours change size gradually and the land widens toward the polar bands, as blue noise, the seeds of the cells by the water moved to the middle of their cells and quickened where the sea cuts their land; the rain is that of a summer and a winter (belts moved by the season, the monsoon from the seas on the equator side, cold and warm currents) and the vote reads both; it learns from the Americas too, without farmland, its pairs weighed so that it reads vanilla's own locations as they are; the ground is voted block by block by the vanilla land nearest in its height, ruggedness, roughness and distance to the sea, every cell taking the votes of the land it covers, and the wasteland plan reads that vote for the kind a cell may be. The relief is worn down to the graded beds of its rivers, its hill country is dissected outside their valley floors and its plateaus are broad tablelands; the ground is voted on the height the decals show, the climate and ground votes are matched to the world's own land, and the wasteland plan ranks the cells by the ruggedness of their ground. Raw materials are drawn from classes pooled with their broader ones by how many vanilla locations stand behind them, calibrated to vanilla's own counts. The location templates, the hierarchy, the localization in all eleven languages and the files that draw them change; the count stays 884.
